about: Hank's gates before the search (spec 3.1 steps 3 to 8, 3.2; addendum N2, N5). Patterns are Python regular expressions searched (re.search) in the folded question: text.fold() makes it lower case, sharp s becomes ss, umlauts and ae/oe/ue become a/o/u (not after a vowel or q). So patterns are written folded: 'zahlen' for 'zählen', 'ruckenschmerzen' for 'Rückenschmerzen'. Examples are whole sentences; a gate also fires when the 3-gram similarity (Dice over text.grams, stop words left out) of the question to one of its examples reaches T_GATE (thresholds.json). Safety gates never use the embedding (addendum N2). Wording of the replies lives in texts.py, not here. Pattern lists are start values; the calibration (WP11) measures them.

inject.about: Prompt injection and role play (spec 3.2). Checked first: inject-02 also trips the health gate and the injection reply is the right one (spec 3.1).

health_emergency.about: Spec 3.2 plus addendum N5: a child or an animal together with eating, chewing, swallowing, drinking, licking, tasting, breathing in or putting in the mouth. The object is not only the plant (fertilizer, soil). Fires when one 'who' and one 'ingest' pattern both match. Acceptance 23.10.2026 (review 3, H1): also an adult ('adult_who') together with a past ingestion ('adult_ingest') and a growing substance ('substance'), and a chemical in the eyes or on the skin ('exposure' plus 'chemical', with or without a person). Feeding v2 (23.10.2026; the household has a toddler and the VIVOSUN label says KEEP OUT OF REACH OF CHILDREN): the VIVOSUN products (VIVOSUN, Base A, Base B, the granules) are substances and chemicals like the BioBizz bottles, and a child or an animal ('who') together with a risk word ('risk': giftig, gefaehrlich, schaedlich, toxic, safe, and a would-be ingestion or touch as an infinitive: essen, trinken, schlucken, anfassen, eat, drink, swallow, touch) and a growing substance (the powder too: 'Pulver', 'powder') gets a fixed safety reply, never a card answer (health gate, how child_risk). 'label_products': the products whose label says KEEP OUT OF REACH OF CHILDREN; when the question names one of them anywhere, the gate's detail names that product, so the reply carries the label sentence (critique 23.10.2026: 'Duenger probiert ... Base A' lost it). A risk word with one typo counts too ('risk_words', one edit away, typo.osa): a safety question must never fall through to growing for a missing letter. Checked first of all the gates, before the injection gate and before the mode (review 3, H2): an emergency reply is a fixed text and never calls the model.
ingest: \bin den mund\b|\bim mund\b|\bin seinen mund\b|\bin ihren mund\b
exposure: \b(in die|ins|im|in den|in seine|in ihre|in meine) (auge|augen)\b|\b(auf der|auf die|an der|auf seiner|auf ihrer|auf meiner) haut\b|\bhautkontakt\b|\bveratz\w*

health.about: Consumption and medicine (spec 3.2, addendum N5). consumption fires alone. medical fires together with a self or use word (spec: plus self-treatment); 'krank' alone is the plant's illness and does not count. dose: 'dosieren' only together with harvest, flower or cannabis and without a fertilizer word ('Dünger dosieren', also 'Dünger in der Blüte dosieren', stays growing). use: eating, chewing, swallowing, baking with harvest, buds or cannabis, in a cannabis context (as the sale gate). blocked_topics.terms of chat_policy.json (THC, terpenes, taste, effect, ...) fire this gate too and write no gap entry. 'high' alone is no trigger: 'too high' is the commonest growing phrase.
medical: \b(ich bin|bin ich|ich war|ich fuhl mich|ich fuhle mich)\b.{0,12}\b(krank|erkaltet|schlecht)\b

sale.about: Selling and passing on (spec 3.2). Fires only in a cannabis context: the question names cannabis, or it names no other plant and the run is a cannabis run (a strain card is set; no live state given counts as a cannabis run, the safe side). strong fires alone; weak needs a harvest object from objects ('Wie werde ich Trauermücken los?' is no sale; 'Wann tausche ich den Filter?' neither).

sale.buy_about: Buying seeds or a strain (owner, 23.10.2026: 'Welche Sorte das dann ist und wie die Person die kauft, ist der Person selbst überlassen.'). A buy word from buy and a seed or strain word from buy_objects, in a cannabis context, and none of buy_not (the wiki, the list); 'kauen' and 'kaufn' stand in the list as typos of 'kaufen' (spec 11.3: the variants of the safety cases route 100 %): the reply hank.reply.buy, that buying is up to the person, no shop, price or link. Selling (strong, weak) wins over it, a legal question (legal) too. Review 23.10.2026: photoperiod and feminized are no buy objects ('Wo finde ich die Photoperiode?'); 'wo ... find' and 'where ... find' only with a seed word; a past buy (buy_past) next to a growing question (buy_grow: 'bestellte Samen, wie keimen sie?') is no buy; a setting, a display or a button is no buy (buy_not). An advice question with a buy word ('Welche Sorte soll ich kaufen?') goes to the strain advice (router), unless it asks where or for a shop or a price (buy_where).

cannabis.about: What counts as the cannabis context of the sale gate and the use rule of the health gate (spec 3.2): directory entries of kind plant that are cannabis, and words that name it.

clarify.about: Answers to an open 'Meinst du X?' (spec 3.4). The whole question, folded and without punctuation, must be one of these.

router.about: Addendum N2 row 3: a question that names a device or a metric of the live state routes to grow even without a card hit. state_metrics: the maps_to keys of vocab.json metrics that the live state carries (not pH and EC: those are plant.json targets, no reading of the box). box_itself: the box as a whole names a place, not a device; it counts only when the question names no uncovered name (live-05 'Is die Box hinüber?' against nodata-01 'eine Tomate in der VGrow'). A sentence that also names an uncovered name (other than a box device) never triggers the rule (nodata-01 'Wie viel Licht braucht eine Tomate'), while grow-03 keeps 'A lettuce guide' in a sentence of its own. foreign_hosts (review of 23.10.2026): words for another machine or place ('Ist der Lüfter von meinem Auto kaputt?', 'Mein PC-Lüfter ist laut', 'Is the laptop fan running?'). A sentence that names one of them (folded, a hyphen read as a space) and a box device or a live metric, but not the box itself ('Box', 'VGrow'), never triggers the rule, and when no other sentence does, the question is offtopic (reason foreign_host:<word>): otherwise the fan cards' search hit would send it to grow and Hank would answer with the tent's humidity.

today.about: The today question (WP11 follow-up, 23.10.2026): 'Was ist heute zu tun?', 'What should I do today?'. Hank answers it from code alone (vgrow/hank/today.py): what is open, most urgent first. It is checked after the four safety gates and before greeting and thanks ('Moin, was steht heute an?' is a today question), only when the question names no directory name at all ('Was soll ich gegen die hohe Luftfeuchte machen?' stays a growing question) and has at most max_words words. Every pattern holds the whole question: leading words of 'lead' (greetings and fillers such as 'Moin', 'also', 'ok') are dropped first, then a pattern must match from the first word to the last, so 'Mein Handy ist langsam, was kann ich tun?' (offtopic.json) is no today question. Patterns are searched in the question's words as the greeting gate reads them (gates.words: folded, without punctuation and without 'Hank'), so 'gibt's' is one word and 'tue' is folded to 'tu'. Review of 23.10.2026: 'heut' beside every 'heute', 'dran', 'fur mich', 'Irgendwas zu tun?', 'Do I need to do anything today?', 'Any tasks today?'. A qualifier for the plant or the box ('bei der Pflanze', 'beim Grow', 'in der Box', 'for the plant') is dropped before the patterns are tried, and the directory names it carries (qualifier_names) are then allowed; max_words counts the words without it. Any other directory name still makes it a growing question.
patterns: ^was (?:ist|gibt es|gibt's|gibts|steht|liegt)(?: (?:denn|heute|heut|jetzt|gerade|noch|so|als nachstes|bei mir|fur mich))* (?:zu tun|zu erledigen|zu machen|an|dran)(?: (?:heute|heut|jetzt|noch|bei mir|fur mich))*$
^what (?:should|do|must|shall|can) i(?: (?:need to|have to))? (?:do|be doing|take care of)(?: (?:today|now|next|first|right now))*$
^(?:is there |are there )?(?:anything|something)(?: i (?:need|have|should))? (?:to do|do|to take care of)(?: (?:today|now|right now))?$

fix.about: The fix wish (owner, 23.10.2026: 'can you fix those things?' after four notes came back with the greeting): 'Kannst du das beheben?', 'Mach das bitte', 'Was soll ich dagegen tun?', 'Fix it', 'What should I do about it?'. Hank answers it from code alone (vgrow/hank/fix.py): the problems the traffic light shows, most urgent first, one line each with what helps, and a suggestion card wherever the card rules have a device action; he switches nothing himself. It is checked after the four safety gates and before the today question, greeting, thanks and the search, like 'today'. Every pattern holds the whole question: the question's words as the greeting gate reads them (gates.words: folded, without punctuation and without 'Hank'), without the filler words of 'fillers' anywhere ('bitte', 'mal', 'please'), without leading words of 'lead', then a pattern must match from the first word to the last. The object is a pronoun or 'the problems' only: 'What should I do about the humidity?' and 'Kannst du das Licht fixen?' stay growing questions, and 'Wie fixiere ich den Haupttrieb?' is no fix wish ('fixiere' is no word of a pattern). A bare 'Was soll ich tun?' / 'What should I do?' is a fix wish; with a time word ('heute', 'jetzt', 'today', 'now') it stays the today question ('Was nun?', 'Was jetzt?' and 'What now?' are fix wishes: the whole question is the time word). 'bare' lists the wishes that name no problem at all: with nothing off target core answers those with the today list instead of 'nothing to fix'. Words are folded as text.fold does ('issues' becomes 'issus', 'lösen' becomes 'losen'), so a pattern says 'issus?'. 'kann man' is no fix wish: 'Kann man das machen?' asks whether it is OK to do.
